label: input w at original position 1 or 2
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is w at original-phase step 1 or 2 (the second or third original token), and nowhere else in practice. Every such step is active, with no false positives. Magnitude is highest at t=1 when the preceding token is i (about 1.0 of max); typical t=1 activations are about 0.8 and t=2 activations about 0.7 to 0.8, so later position slightly lowers it. It does not fire on w at t=0 or at t>=3 (apart from 39 tiny activations at t=3 after v w), on any other token, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (22 weak activations of about 0.06 to 0.1 when w is fed back at step 5).

issues: Minor wording issue: the explanation says the few tiny t=3 activations come 'after v w'. That holds on the dev split (p w v w, k e v w, ...). On the test split the t=3 misses mostly follow k-initial prefixes instead (p k k w, k k x w, k e y w, k k 2 w), all at activation 0.03-0.04. These are negligible in mass (0.0%) and do not form a meaningful class.
Copy-phase claim confirmed: 22 dev activations, all at step 5 when w is fed back (seen in L=3 sequences), at 0.04-0.10. Negligible.
Test scores reproduce: precision 1.0, recall 0.9985, F1 0.9993, mass recall 0.9999, correlation 0.996. There are 0 false positives on both dev and test.

Magnitude claims confirmed. The top activations (1.00) are all 'i w' at t=1. The t=1 cases with other previous tokens sit around 0.80-0.83, and t=2 around 0.68-0.79. Activation does not fire at t=0 and is essentially absent at t>=3.
